record.paper_title: Approximating network dynamics: Some open problems
record.original_question: Formulate and prove the broadest possible abstract versions of Theorems 4.2 and 4.3, isolating the general bifurcation structure and time-scale-separation mechanisms that are really needed for consistency or strong consistency between Boolean systems and their ODE realizations.

evidence.quote: While the proofs of Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 given in [20] rely on the particular details of the intrinsic dynamics of the signature variables, the author of this note believes that they should remain valid for broader classes of ODE models. Problem 5. Formulate and prove versions of Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 in an abstract setting that is as general as possible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a finite directed network (interaction graph) with node set $V=\{1,\dots,n\}$. To each node $i$ associate a real-valued state variable $x_i(t)$ governed by an ODE system
$$\dot x_i = F_i(x_1,\dots,x_n;\lambda),\qquad i=1,\dots,n,$$
where $\lambda$ is a (vector) parameter, and the $F_i$ are sufficiently smooth functions whose dependence on $x_j$ respects the directed edges of the network. Assume that for each $i$ there is a finite set of thresholds $\theta_{i,1}<\dots<\theta_{i,k_i}$ partitioning the $x_i$-axis, inducing a discretization map
$$\Pi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\prod_{i=1}^{n}\{0,1,\dots,k_i\},\qquad \Pi(x)_i = \#\{\ell:\theta_{i,\ell}\le x_i\}.$$
A Boolean (or multi-level) discrete dynamical system $\Phi:\prod_i\{0,\dots,k_i\}\to\prod_i\{0,\dots,k_i\}$ is said to be a discrete realization of the ODE system if it is constructed from the network structure together with the monotonicity pattern of the $F_i$ on each rectangular cell of the threshold partition.

Definitions of consistency. Say that the discrete system $\Phi$ is consistent with the ODE flow $\varphi^t_\lambda$ if for every recurrent attractor $A$ of $\Phi$ (e.g. a fixed point or a periodic cycle of $\Phi$) there exists, for an open set of parameters $\lambda$, an invariant set $A_\lambda$ of $\varphi^t_\lambda$ such that $\Pi(A_\lambda)\subseteq A$ and the dynamics of $\varphi^t_\lambda$ restricted to $A_\lambda$ projects onto the dynamics of $\Phi$ on $A$. Say that $\Phi$ is strongly consistent with $\varphi^t_\lambda$ if, in addition, every $\omega$-limit set of $\varphi^t_\lambda$ projects under $\Pi$ into a recurrent set of $\Phi$.

Two consistency theorems (concrete form). Suppose the intrinsic node dynamics consist of so-called "signature variables" exhibiting (a) a saddle–node-type bifurcation structure as the aggregate input crosses node-specific thresholds, and (b) a separation of time-scales between fast intrinsic relaxation and slow inter-node coupling. Under these hypotheses one can prove:

(T1) The discrete realization $\Phi$ is consistent with $\varphi^t_\lambda$ for all sufficiently large time-scale separation.
(T2) Under additional monotonicity and non-degeneracy conditions on the bifurcation diagrams of the intrinsic dynamics, $\Phi$ is strongly consistent with $\varphi^t_\lambda$.

Problem. Identify the most general abstract hypotheses on the family $\{F_i\}$ — phrased purely in terms of (i) a qualitative bifurcation structure of the intrinsic single-node dynamics as the coupling input varies, and (ii) a singular-perturbation / time-scale-separation mechanism between intrinsic and coupling terms — under which the analogues of (T1) and (T2) hold. Formulate and prove versions of (T1) and (T2) at this level of generality, removing any reliance on the specific functional form of the signature variables, and exhibit broad classes of ODE network models (beyond the original neuroscience-motivated example) to which the abstract theorems apply.
artifact.category_tag: Boolean approximations of ODE network dynamics
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem about generalizing two specific consistency theorems between Boolean/discrete approximations and ODE realizations of network dynamics. Recent literature on DSGRN and Boolean-ODE correspondences continues to develop concrete consistency results in special settings, but no general abstract version isolating the minimal bifurcation and time-scale-separation hypotheses appears to have been published. Status: apparently still open.

status_evidence.title: Approximating network dynamics: Some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Outlines open problems on structural features of ODE models that allow for the construction of discrete approximations whose predictions are consistent with those of the ODE models.
status_evidence.claim: The general abstract version of the consistency theorems is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: DSGRN: Examining the Dynamics of Families of Logical Models
status_evidence.snippet: DSGRN associates to a network an ODE model with piece-wise constant monotone nonlinearities; ODE solutions are described by a finite state transition graph.
status_evidence.claim: Existing consistency results between discrete state transition graphs and ODE flows remain restricted to specific (e.g. piecewise-constant or switching) classes.

status_evidence.title: Subnetwork inclusion and switching of multilevel Boolean networks
status_evidence.snippet: Multilevel Boolean networks preserving parameter graph structure and dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to develop discrete-ODE correspondences in specific frameworks rather than offering a fully abstract consistency theorem.
